prerequisites: knowledge of basic concepts of stresses and strains (from strength of materials)
strength and stiffness of materials (from materials science)

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the different concepts and quantities from continuum mechanics and the relationships between these quantities.
The student can write down the complete set of equations for an elastic and an elasto-plastic analysis of an arbitrary body in a two- or three-dimensional space.
The student can interpret a stress and strain state.
The student knows the techniques for converting analytical equations into numerical simulation techniques.

The student is able to independently perform an analytical elaboration of a continuum mechanical problem with an elastic material and a simple geometry in a two- or three-dimensional space, and with an elasto-plastic material in a one- or two-dimensional domain.
The student can calculate the displacements of the deformed body, as well as the strain components and stresses.
The student can interpret a complex spatial stress and strain state.
The student learns to work with commercial finite element software and learns to interpret the results of an analysis.

syllabus_topics: stress tensor in a coordinate transformation
principal directions of the stress tensor
Lagrangian and Eulerian description of displacement and deformation
physical meaning of the strain tensor: change in length and change in angle
principal directions of the strain tensor
constitutive law for a linear isotropic elastic material
constitutive law for hydrostatic and deviatoric stress components
constitutive equations in a transformed coordinate system
material models for elastic materials: anisotropic, with one plane of symmetry, orthotropic, transversely isotropic
2D stress states in Cartesian coordinates: plane stress state, plane strain state, Airy's stress function
2D stress states in polar coordinates: relationship between displacements and strain components, Airy's stress function
repetition of virtual displacements of rigid bodies
virtual work in virtual displacements for elastic continua: virtual work of external and internal forces
theorem of virtual work and equivalence with equilibrium
virtual work in virtual forces for elastic continua: virtual work of external and internal forces
theorem of complementary virtual work and equivalence with compatibility
concepts of potential energy: potential energy of external forces, elastic energy and potential functions of energy density
theorem of minimum potential energy: 1st variation and equilibrium, 2nd variation and stability
theorem of stationary complementary energy: equivalence with compatibility
kinematics of thin flat plates under transverse loading, Kirchhoff's hypothesis
stress resultants in thin flat plates
equilibrium equations: plate equation and boundary conditions
application to bending of a beam in plastic regime
2. Yield criteria in two- and three-dimensional stress states
general form of the yield criterion
yield criteria for ductile materials: Tresca, von Mises
fracture criteria for brittle materials: Mohr-Coulomb
normality of the plastic deformation increment to the yield surface
Structure-mechanical problems in a two-dimensional space:
determination of principal stresses, principal strains, and principal directions for a given stress tensor
calculation of stress components that are decisive for yield criteria
calculation of stress fields using stress functions
Structure-mechanical problems in a three-dimensional space:
determination of principal stresses, principal strains, and principal directions for a given stress tensor
calculation of stress components that are decisive for yield criteria
Plates: calculation of the deflection of a plate using Ritz's approximation method
Pressure cylinders in an elasto-plastic deformation situation:
calculation of the elasto-plastic stress distribution
assessment_rules: The exam is written with an oral explanation. Each student receives three questions: one theory question (a derivation), one exercise from the elasticity part, and one exercise from the plasticity part. For the theory question and one of the exercises, there is an individual oral discussion after written preparation. The third question is only assessed in writing. The weighting for the three questions is equal. Rounding follows the usual rule, but if there are insufficient marks on at least two of the three questions, rounding is always downwards.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
